subsystems.name: Optical sensing array
subsystems.role: shines light into the skin and detects the faint signal scattered back, aiming to infer biomarker concentrations.

subsystems.name: Skin interface
subsystems.role: keeps the optical path stable against the skin so measurements are repeatable despite movement and varying skin tones.

subsystems.name: Signal processing and calibration
subsystems.role: converts raw optical readings into estimates of glucose and cortisol using models trained against blood references.

subsystems.name: Power and connectivity
subsystems.role: runs the ring for days and sends data to a phone.

subsystems.name: Ring housing
subsystems.role: protects the electronics and fits comfortably on a finger.

subsystems.name: Companion app
subsystems.role: shows trends and gives metabolic-health guidance.

buildSteps.title: Choose the spectroscopy method
buildSteps.detail: Compare near-infrared, Raman and photoacoustic approaches for signal strength, skin penetration and how well they can be miniaturised into a ring.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the sensor module
buildSteps.detail: Integrate light sources, detectors and filters on a substrate small enough to fit inside a ring, while keeping optical alignment precise.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical path
buildSteps.detail: Use lenses, light guides and filters to direct light into the skin and collect scattered light efficiently from a consistent depth.

buildSteps.title: Collect paired training data
buildSteps.detail: Record optical signals while volunteers also use a blood draw or an invasive continuous glucose monitor, building a dataset that links light to biomarker levels.

buildSteps.title: Train calibration algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Apply machine learning to separate the weak biomarker signal from noise caused by skin, blood flow, temperature and movement.

buildSteps.title: Validate in clinical studies
buildSteps.detail: Test the ring against venous blood measurements across meals, exercise and sleep, checking accuracy for different people and skin types.

buildSteps.title: Miniaturise the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Shrink the processor, battery and radio into the ring while managing heat and power use.

buildSteps.title: Clear regulatory approval
buildSteps.detail: Gain approval as a medical device for glucose monitoring, which is required before any health claims can be made.

prerequisites.why: small LEDs and photodiodes are already used in wearables for heart rate and oxygen.
no optical method has yet proven reliable enough for clinical use outside the lab.
cortisol is present at very low, rapidly changing levels that optical signals cannot yet isolate.
models can extract signals from complex spectra, but they need large, diverse training sets and can fail on new users.
small batteries and Bluetooth are already standard in smart rings and watches.

pathway.milestone: research labs test optical and other non-invasive glucose methods; smart rings track heart rate, temperature and sleep
pathway.unlocks: a base of wearable hardware and data pipelines.

pathway.milestone: controlled pilot studies show a ring can track glucose trends closely enough to be useful
first commercial ring cleared for non-invasive glucose monitoring
multi-analyte rings that also estimate cortisol, lactate and other markers
